data.title: .gitignore
data.tagline: Tell Git which untracked files should stay out of version control
data.description: .gitignore patterns keep generated files, dependencies, local settings, and secrets from being added by accident. It does not remove files that are already tracked, and it should not replace secure secret management.

use: Keep local environment files out of commits
avoid: Assume it removes a file already committed
Ignore source files just to hide an accidental change
Commit a secret first and add it to .gitignore later
Use broad patterns without checking what else they match

lessonPractice.title: A real .env was already committed and pushed before being added to .gitignore. What else must happen?

options.label: Stop tracking it, keep a secret-free example, and immediately rotate exposed credentials
options.feedback: Ignore rules affect untracked content only, and credentials exposed in history must be revoked and replaced.

options.label: Commit only .gitignore and assume the old file and secret disappear from history
options.feedback: Tracked files do not vanish from a new rule, and prior commit content remains.

options.label: Keep using the old secret because .gitignore has now encrypted and hidden it
options.feedback: Gitignore is a matching rule, not encryption for committed or local content.

data.agentPrompt: Check whether .env is tracked; if committed, stop tracking it, add it to .gitignore, and keep a value-free .env.example. List and rotate every exposed credential, and never treat ignore rules as history removal or encryption.
